nodes.label: Mars
nodes.description: The fourth planet from the Sun, known as the Red Planet. Mars has a thin atmosphere, polar ice caps, and evidence of past liquid water. Its surface area equals Earth's land area.

nodes.label: Olympus Mons
nodes.description: The largest volcano in the Solar System, standing 22 km high with a diameter of 624 km. Located in the Tharsis region.

nodes.label: Valles Marineris
nodes.description: A vast canyon system stretching 4,000 km long, up to 7 km deep, and 200 km wide. The largest canyon in the Solar System.

nodes.label: Gale Crater
nodes.description: Impact crater 154 km in diameter, site of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons). Landing site of Curiosity rover. Contains ancient lakebed deposits.

nodes.label: Jezero Crater
nodes.description: 45 km diameter crater with an ancient river delta. Landing site of Perseverance rover. Contains carbonate and clay minerals suggesting past habitability.

nodes.label: Tharsis Region
nodes.description: Volcanic plateau hosting three large shield volcanoes (Ascraeus, Pavonis, Arsia Montes) near Olympus Mons. Influenced Mars' climate history.

nodes.label: Hellas Planitia
nodes.description: Large impact basin 2,300 km in diameter and 7 km deep. One of the lowest elevations on Mars, potentially hosting seasonal brines.

nodes.label: Utopia Planitia
nodes.description: Large plain in the northern lowlands. Landing site of Viking 2. Contains subsurface ice detected by radar.

nodes.label: Planum Australe
nodes.description: The south polar plateau. Site of the MARSIS-discovered subglacial liquid water lake (Orosei et al. 2018).

nodes.label: Terra Cimmeria
nodes.description: Ancient terrain with strong crustal magnetic anomalies, evidence of Mars' former dynamo. Key area for paleomagnetic studies.

nodes.label: Medusae Fossae F.
nodes.description: Large enigmatic geological formation of fine-grained, easily eroded material. Possibly volcanic ash deposits. Contains significant water ice.

nodes.label: Arabia Terra
nodes.description: Densely cratered highland region in the northern hemisphere. Contains layered deposits and evidence of ancient aqueous activity.

nodes.label: Elysium Mons
nodes.description: Volcanic province in the eastern hemisphere. Second largest volcanic region after Tharsis. Contains frozen lava flows.

nodes.label: Viking 1 & 2
nodes.description: NASA's 1976 mission. First successful landers on Mars. Viking 1 landed at Chryse Planitia, Viking 2 at Utopia Planitia. Conducted life detection experiments.

nodes.label: Mars Pathfinder
nodes.description: NASA's 1997 mission. First successful rover (Sojourner). Demonstrated airbag landing technology at Ares Vallis.

nodes.label: Spirit & Opportunity
nodes.description: NASA's twin MER rovers, landed 2004. Spirit explored Gusev Crater; Opportunity found evidence of past water at Meridiani Planum. Opp. operated until 2018.

nodes.label: Phoenix Lander
nodes.description: NASA's 2008 lander at Vastitas Borealis. First to confirm perchlorates in Martian soil (~0.4-0.6 wt%). Observed falling snow and frost.

nodes.label: Curiosity (MSL)
nodes.description: NASA's car-sized rover, landed 2012 at Gale Crater. Investigates past habitability. Discovered complex organic molecules and seasonal methane variations.

nodes.label: InSight Lander
nodes.description: NASA's 2018 geophysical lander near Elysium Planitia. First to detect marsquakes via SEIS. Measured crust thickness ~24-72 km. HP3 heat probe deployment had difficulties.

nodes.label: Perseverance
nodes.description: NASA's 2021 rover at Jezero Crater. Collects samples for Mars Sample Return. Carries Ingenuity helicopter. Detected organics at Wildcat Ridge.

nodes.label: MAVEN
nodes.description: NASA orbiter since 2014. Studies Mars' upper atmosphere and atmospheric escape to understand climate evolution. Measures solar wind interaction.

nodes.label: MRO
nodes.description: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, NASA, since 2006. Carries HiRISE and CRISM. High-resolution imaging and mineral mapping. Discovered recurring slope lineae.

nodes.label: Mars Express
nodes.description: ESA orbiter since 2003. Carries HRSC, MARSIS, OMEGA. Discovered subglacial liquid water lake at south pole (2018).

nodes.label: 2001 Mars Odyssey
nodes.description: NASA orbiter since 2001. Longest-operating Mars spacecraft. Maps mineral distribution and serves as communication relay.

nodes.label: Ingenuity
nodes.description: First powered, controlled aircraft on another planet. 72 flights on Mars (2021-2024). Demonstrated aerial exploration capability.

nodes.label: SAM
nodes.description: Sample Analysis at Mars, aboard Curiosity. Pyrolysis-GC-MS instrument suite. Detected chlorobenzene (150-300 ppbw), thiophenes, and seasonal methane.

nodes.label: SHERLOC
nodes.description: Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals, aboard Perseverance. Fluorescence/Raman spectroscopy for organic detection.

nodes.label: CRISM
nodes.description: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars, aboard MRO. Visible/near-infrared spectrometer for hydrated mineral mapping.

nodes.label: HiRISE
nodes.description: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment, aboard MRO. 0.3 m/pixel camera. Cataloged thousands of dust devils, imaged recurring slope lineae.

nodes.label: HRSC
nodes.description: High Resolution Stereo Camera, aboard Mars Express. Produces 3D terrain models and full-color images of the Martian surface.

nodes.label: MARSIS
nodes.description: Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding, aboard Mars Express. Subsurface radar. Discovered subglacial liquid water at south pole (Orosei et al. 2018).

nodes.label: OMEGA
nodes.description: Observatoire pour la Minéralogie, l'Eau, les Glaces et l'Activité, aboard Mars Express. Visible/near-infrared mineral mapping spectrometer.

nodes.label: SEIS
nodes.description: Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure, aboard InSight. First seismometer on Mars. Detected 1,300+ marsquakes. Largest: M4.7 in 2022.

nodes.label: WCL
nodes.description: Wet Chemistry Lab, aboard Phoenix. First confirmed detection of perchlorates (Mg(ClO4)2) in Martian soil, ~0.4-0.6 wt% (Hecht et al. 2009).

nodes.label: SuperCam
nodes.description: Aboard Perseverance. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy, Raman, infrared, and microphone. First direct evidence of electrical discharges in dust devils.

nodes.label: MEDA
nodes.description: Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer, aboard Perseverance. Measures temperature, wind, pressure, humidity, and dust properties.

nodes.label: Perchlorates
nodes.description: Strong oxidants (ClO4-) found in Martian soil. First confirmed by Phoenix WCL. Degrade organics when heated. Present at ~0.4-0.6 wt% in northern plains.

nodes.label: Organic Molecules
nodes.description: Complex organic compounds detected by Curiosity SAM (chlorobenzene, thiophenes, aromatics) and Perseverance SHERLOC. Preserved in ancient sedimentary rocks for billions of years.

nodes.label: Transient Brines
nodes.description: Saline liquid water that may exist transiently on Mars. Perchlorate brines could be stable under specific temperature and humidity conditions. Not yet directly detected.

nodes.label: Dust Devils
nodes.description: Convective vortices common on Mars. Generate electric fields via tribocharging. Thousands cataloged by HiRISE. Can loft dust to several km altitude.

nodes.label: Subglacial Water
nodes.description: Liquid water lake discovered beneath south polar ice cap by MARSIS (Orosei et al. 2018, Science). Located at Planum Australe / Ultimi Scopuli region.

nodes.label: Crustal Magnetism
nodes.description: Remanent magnetic anomalies in ancient crust, especially Terra Cimmeria. Evidence of a former global magnetic field and dynamo that shut down ~4 billion years ago.

nodes.label: Methane Variability
nodes.description: Trace methane detected by Curiosity SAM with seasonal variations (~0.4 ppb background, spikes to ~7 ppb). Origin unknown: biological, geological, or exogenic.

nodes.label: Recurring Slope Lineae
nodes.description: Dark streaks on steep slopes appearing seasonally. Initially hypothesized as liquid water flows. Current consensus favors dry granular flows. Detected by HiRISE.

nodes.label: Atmosphere
nodes.description: Thin CO2-dominated atmosphere (~95% CO2, 2.8% N2, 2% Ar). Surface pressure ~0.6% of Earth's. Seasonal polar cap exchange of CO2. Studied by MAVEN for escape processes.

nodes.label: Regolith
nodes.description: Layer of loose, fragmented material covering bedrock. Contains perchlorates, basaltic minerals, and amorphous material. Electrostatic charging affects dust transport.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal Systems
nodes.description: Ancient hydrothermal environments evidenced by mineral assemblages (silica, clays, sulfates). Potential habitats for past microbial life. Studied by Spirit at Home Plate.

nodes.label: Climate Evolution
nodes.description: Mars transitioned from a warmer, wetter past to a cold, dry present. Atmospheric loss to space driven by solar wind (studied by MAVEN). CO2 cycle creates seasonal pressure changes.

nodes.label: Impact Processes
nodes.description: Cratering has shaped Mars' surface and potentially created transient hydrothermal systems. Impact shock can drive redox reactions. Studied in Arabia Terra and Hellas.

nodes.label: Q001: Dust Devils & Organics
nodes.description: Do Martian dust devils selectively transport and concentrate specific organic compounds in the atmosphere? AI-generated novel question about atmospheric organic chemistry.

nodes.label: Q002: Regolith Charging & Brines
nodes.description: Does the Martian regolith's electrostatic charging alter the stability of subsurface brines and their potential for hosting life?

nodes.label: Q003: Impact Redox Gradients
nodes.description: Do Martian impact craters create localized electrochemical gradients driving redox reactions between perchlorates and organics?

nodes.label: Q004: CO2 Frost Electrochemistry
nodes.description: Do seasonal CO2 frost deposits create transient electrochemical environments that facilitate non-biological synthesis of complex organics?

nodes.label: Q005: Microtopography & Water
nodes.description: Do Martian microtopographic features create localized microclimates influencing transient liquid water film stability?

nodes.label: Q006: Ionosphere & Organics
nodes.description: Does ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling generate anomalous EM fields that influence subsurface organics distribution?

nodes.label: Q007: Crustal Magnetism & Life
nodes.description: Does crustal magnetic field generate electrochemical environments driving redox reactions, creating subsurface oases for chemosynthetic life?
